- Training status: advanced lifter

- Primary goals (implied): maintain/build strength, support bone density, manage vasomotor symptoms and recovery, maintain body composition and general conditioning

Overview and coaching aims
- Emphasise progressive resistance training with bone-loading (impact, heavy eccentrics when tolerated), multi-joint strength as primary focus. Because client is advanced, program will use heavy sets, reverse periodisation for strength and power, then hypertrophy and consolidation.
- Respect vasomotor symptoms: schedule intense/conditioning sessions during coolest parts of day, avoid prolonged high-heat exposures, include cooling strategies pre/during/post session (cooling vest/ice towel, fans, cold drinks), and avoid fasted HIIT in hot conditions. - Nutritional targets: protein 1.4–2.0 g/kg/day (aim 1.6–1.8), distribute protein across meals (20–40 g per meal), adequate calcium (1000–1300 mg/day) and vitamin D (check labs; typical maintenance 800–2000 IU/day unless prescribed otherwise). Ensure energy intake supports training (avoid long fasted cardio in heat). Manage hydration and electrolytes to reduce vasomotor triggers (small, regular cold fluids).
- Monitoring: RPE, sleep, hot flash frequency/severity, cycle length, mood, body weight/composition (optional), readiness/perceived recovery each week.
- Start date: 2026-06-01. 12 weeks split into 3 phases: Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4) — Base strength, movement quality, heat-acclimating conservatively; Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8) — Strength & power emphasis, slight volume reduction, targeted bone-loading; Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12) — Peak strength and hypertrophy consolidation, tapering conditioning, deload week last week.

General weekly structure (example)
- 4 resistance sessions per week (two heavy lower-body/hip focused, one heavy upper-body, one full-body/hypertrophy or accessory). Advanced lifter can handle intensity and frequency.
- 1 short conditioned session (low-heat interval or conditioning circuit in cool environment) OR low-impact aerobic session (20–30 min) depending on tolerance.
- 1 active recovery session or mobility/conditioning.
- 1 rest day.

Cooling protocol (every training day)
- Pre-session: cool shower or apply cold pack to neck/upper back 10–15 min; hydrate with cold beverage 250–500 ml in 30 min pre-workout.
- During: fan directed at client, cold towel/ice pack on neck between heavy sets, keep training area well-ventilated/air-conditioned, breathing and pacing to minimize hot flash triggers.
- Post: cold drink, cool shower if needed, loose clothing, lie in cooler environment for 10–15 min.

- Weeks 1–4: establish technique, 3–5RM work, build CNS readiness; 3–4 sets of heavy lifts + accessory volume.
- Weeks 5–8: increase intensity (up to 85–92% 1RM for singles/doubles on main lifts), introduce power/intended velocity (low-heat, not fasted), bone-loading (drops, controlled landings if tolerated).
- Weeks 9–11: heavier compound focus with some volume for hypertrophy (6–12 reps on accessory), peak week 11; Week 12: deload/recovery (reduced volume 40–60%, intensity down).
